newsitem.title: UK: Medeva says to regain rights over Ionamin.
newsitem.headline: Medeva says to regain rights over Ionamin.

text.p: Britain's Medeva Plc said on Wednesday it had reached "an early and satisfactory resolution" of its dispute with Resolve Medical Marketing Inc of the U.S. over marketing rights to its anti-obesity drug Ionamin.

Medeva said in a statement it would regain full control of marketing rights to the product. Resolve had been receiving commissions of 47 1/2 percent on sales of Ionamin, a drug which Medeva acquired with the U.S. assets of drugs group Fisons last year.
In a statement, Medeva said, however, that buoyant sales of Ionamin in the second half of 1996 had not continued into the first half of 1997, with sales slipping to seven million stg from 22 million.
The market for anti-obesity drugs has been hit by a number of health scares, including worries over heart valve problems.
"A recovery in Ionamin sales in the short term seems unlikely despite support from our full-time sales force which began in May," the company said.

Medeva also announced the acquisition of a Belgian marketing company, CERTA, for 4 million stg, which it said helped to extend its European sales structure and give it a foothold in the Benelux countries.
The company also announced a distribution agreement with Germany's Fresenius AG covering 20 European countries for its anaesthetic gases.
